title: Handwashing, dishes and cleaning without running water
summary: Wash with soap for 20 seconds, use 60% alcohol sanitizer only as a backup, and sanitize dishes with bleach.

sources.title: CDC: Guidelines for Personal Hygiene During an Emergency
CDC: Keep Food Safe After a Disaster or Emergency
CDC: Drinking Water Advisories: An Overview

blocks.text: Clean hands and clean dishes stop stomach illness, which spreads fast when water is short.

items: **Wet** your hands with clean water. Soap up.
**Lather** the backs of your hands, between fingers and under nails.
**Rinse** with clean water and **dry** with a clean towel.

blocks.text: No running tap? Set up a handwashing station: a large jug of clean water you can pour from, plus soap. During a boil-water advisory, soap and tap water are often fine for handwashing, but follow your local officials. If told to be extra careful, use boiled or disinfected water.

**Wash hands:** before, during and after preparing food. Before eating. After the toilet. After diapers. After caring for someone vomiting or with diarrhea. After touching garbage. After coughing, sneezing or blowing your nose.

items: Use only if soap and water aren't available.
It must be **at least 60% alcohol**. Check the label.
It doesn't work well on visibly dirty or greasy hands.
It doesn't remove every germ and **doesn't remove chemicals**.
**Sanitize:** soak for **1 minute** in **1 cup of unscented household bleach per 5 gallons of clean water**. Cover everything.

blocks.text: During a **boil-water advisory**, CDC gives a different mix for handwashing dishes: **1 teaspoon of unscented liquid bleach per gallon of warm water**, soak at least **1 minute**, air dry. A dishwasher is OK if it has a sanitizing cycle or a final rinse of at least **150°F**. Use disposable plates and cups if you can.
For things you can't soak, wipe with a cloth wet with the same **1 cup bleach per 5 gallons** solution. Use only plain unscented bleach.

items: Follow local advice. Water that isn't safe to drink can sometimes be used for bathing, but don't swallow it or get it in your eyes.
**Don't bathe** in flood water, sewage-contaminated water, or rivers, streams or lakes contaminated by floods, sewage or animal waste.
Sponge baths for babies and young children during a boil-water advisory.
